title: Personal Credit Cards: which account may receive the points cash-out of a card being closed
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: receiving account for a closing points cash-out

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line and reads the cardholder's checking accounts. When a cardholder who is closing a card asks to cash out its rewards points, it fixes where the cash-out may go.

## Rule

1. Outside a closing, points may still be redeemed as a deposit to a PCB checking or savings account of the same customer, at the tier's cash value per point.
2. A closing cash-out, however, is made only as a deposit to a PCB checking account of the cardholder whose status is active, the account the cardholder names.
3. A savings deposit, a statement credit, a gift card or travel is not a closing cash-out under this policy.
4. When the cardholder holds no PCB checking account whose status is active, no closing cash-out can be made, and the points cashed out are 0.

The status is read from the bank's checking account records; the cardholder chooses which of their active checking accounts receives the deposit.

## Decision table

| Destination the cardholder asks for | May receive a closing cash-out under this policy |
|---|---|
| a PCB checking account of the cardholder, active | yes |
| a PCB checking account of the cardholder, not active | no |
| a PCB savings account | no |
| a statement credit on the card | no |
| a gift card or travel | no |

## Points of judgement

- A deposit to a PCB savings account remains a redemption way outside a closing; what it cannot be is a closing cash-out.
- A cardholder with two active PCB checking accounts names the one that receives the cash-out.
- A cardholder whose only checking account is not active cannot make a closing cash-out; the points cashed out are 0.
- The receiving account need not be the card's autopay source, provided it is an active PCB checking account of the cardholder.
